challenge.better_approach: Alternatives looked at: (a) make encapsulation_holds red a breach on every row, which would turn a single breach into a red for every crossing in the system, so one component's defect would stop all the others; (b) put the widening in clearance at PROVED only, which still lets PROVEME and the seal stand on an unjudged component; (c) Q#103's BUILDME lane, which would refuse ticket shapes that write outside their owner. That's an ownership rule, not a measurement, and it's still open. The gate choosing its component set from bounds.in is the smallest change: one function, and the sieves are left alone.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That bounds.in covers what the build actually wrote. A build that writes outside its bounds escapes this gate as well. That's the bounds door's concern, not this one. Also assumed: a component a ticket writes is currently green before the build, so the wider gate doesn't red a ticket for an older defect. Where it does, that red is real and it's already on main (Law 9: there's no 'pre-existing' triage).
challenge.prior_art: In-house: _build_gate (transitions.py:1348) has inspected one comp_dir since 2026-07-27. The memory 'a land leaves another seal stale' records n=2 of the same shape (40e4, 6095), handled by hand. Q#103 (open-212b2de5c6b8, open-7efe6d23d259) is the open ownership question behind the 38-of-177 measurement. No ticket widens the inspected set. Outside the system: CI that checks only the changed package misses breaks in its dependents, and the usual fix is to check every package the change touches.
challenge.real_collision: Q#103 (open-212b2de5c6b8): no exclusive collision. Under 'one ticket per component' this gate inspects just one component, and under 'spanning tickets allowed' it inspects every component the ticket writes. It holds either way, and that's recorded in the constraints.

answers.falsifier: RED if a PROVEME crossing for a ticket owned by A whose bounds.in holds a file in B carrying a cross-device import crosses, or refuses without naming B; RED if a ticket whose bounds.in sit wholly in its owner changes its record shape. Horizon: the next land that writes outside its owner reds at its own crossing, not at the next owner's (n=3 of the other way, measured 40e4, 6095, dda0).
answers.from_idea: none, because the gap was measured live: dda0e72b9c67 crossed PROVED green at cairn 8c3380c06 over a breach its own build c9d4e79f6 wrote, and akiendelllinux:/tmp/claude-1000/-home-akien-dev-src-cairn/546bccde-fde2-48b2-9435-eaf9605f128f/scratchpad/encap_probe.sh reproduces the per-row predicate at that commit
answers.how: In cairn/tools/base/transitions.py _build_gate, when the crossing carries a ticket, map each bounds.in path to its innermost component (longest component_dirs prefix, cairn/tools/base/address.py), run inspect_build over the owning component plus those, refuse on any red with each finding naming its component, and name every inspected component in the note and record. A ticket writing only its owner inspects exactly as today. Red-first proof in cairn/tools/base/proofs/ over a scratch repo with two components.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass): a gate that inspects one of the components a build wrote passes the rest unexamined, and a false green gets leaned on by a peer. RULE 1: the breach it missed was a reach into a device.
answers.what: A ticket's PROVEME build gate runs the build_inspector over every census component holding a path in the ticket's bounds.in, not only the component its owning_intention names, so a red its build writes into another component reds its own crossing.

bullets.text: Measured at 8c3380c06: the breach {source bin, target cairn/devices/tester, line 81} reds on the bin and tester rows and on 0 rows for cairn/tools/scratch, which owns dda0, so dda0 crossed PROVEME and PROVED green.
The pattern 'a land leaves a red at another component's next crossing' is now n=3 (40e4, 6095, dda0); each time, the next ticket's builder paid for it with a bug ticket.

title: A ticket's PROVEME build gate runs the build_inspector over every census component holding a path in the ticket's bounds
